column1: # scripts/check.sh gate portability -- CAN THIS GATE RUN ON A GITHUB RUNNER?
# GENERATED FROM MEASUREMENT, not from reading the sources. Every row was produced by running its

# step in a runner-equivalent checkout -- `git clone --depth 1 --branch
file://`, which
# holds tracked files only and carries no game image, no origin/main, and only *.sample hooks --
# and comparing what it printed there against the developer tree. A static scan for
# `eldenring-deobf` was tried first and was wrong in BOTH directions: 18 gates that name the image
# ran fine without it, and gates that never name it failed. The scan was thrown away.
# THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS is not whether a gate exits 0 -- it is whether it CHECKED anything.
# Fourteen gates print one line saying their input is absent and exit 0, so check.sh wrote `passed`
# beside a gate that had asserted nothing at all. Those are `blocked`, and check.sh now skips them
# out loud. A gate that still carries real PASS lines beside its skip line is `partial` and is
# still run: half of something is coverage, and it says which half it lost.
# WHAT THAT MEASUREMENT CANNOT SEE: it relocates the REPO ROOT and nothing else. $HOME, $PATH and
# the installed toolchain are still the developer's, so a gate that reaches OUTSIDE the checkout
# is measured against a machine no runner resembles and comes back `portable` when it is not.
# One row was wrong for exactly this reason and only the first full CI run found it:
# whose preflight require_file's $HOME/Elden/launch.sh -- the user's real ME3 launcher -- even
# under --dry-run, so it exited 2 on the runner and passed in every clone-based simulation. The
# fix was to make the test hermetic (it now points PRODUCT_LAUNCHER at a fixture), not to demote
# the row, because the gate itself never needed the launcher. When adding a row, read the step
# for $HOME, absolute paths outside the repo, and network or device access; the simulation will
# `scripts/ci-gate-portability.py --check` requires every check.sh step that RUNS a repo script to
# have a row here, and every row to still name a step. That is what stops this classification
# drifting behind the suite the way .github/workflows/check.yml's hand-written step list did.
# Toolchain steps (cargo/shellcheck/rustfmt/opa/cupcake) are deliberately NOT ledgered: their
# dependency is "is the tool installed", which check.sh answers at run time in _check_tool_skip.
# A FIFTH COLUMN WAS ADDED 2026-09-11: which STAGE of scripts/check.sh runs this gate.
# It lives here rather than in a `docs/check-stages.tsv` of its own because this file already holds
# exactly one row per gate step, and `ci-gate-portability.py --check` already keeps that set in
# bijection with check.sh's step list. A second file keyed the same way would be a second key set
# that could disagree with this one, which is the disease rather than the cure. So the row that
# says what external input a gate needs is the row that says which stage runs it: one line to add
# when a gate is written, and one gate to keep both answers honest.
# The stage names are declared in `scripts/check-stages.py`, and `check-stages.py --check` (a step
# of check.sh) refuses a row naming a stage that does not exist, a step in no stage, a step in two,
# and a declared stage that holds no steps. Toolchain steps -- cargo/shellcheck/rustfmt/opa/cupcake
# -- are still not ledgered, and their stage comes from four rules in that file for the same reason
# their portability does not live here: the answer is uniform and identical rows could go stale.
# columns: bucket <TAB> deps <TAB> key <TAB> what it does when the input is absent <TAB> stage
#   portable  ran and passed with no game-derived input present
#   partial   ran, asserted something real, and said which half it could not do. STILL RUN.
#   blocked   asserted nothing (or refused outright). check.sh SKIPS it, loudly, as a non-pass.
#   deps      '-' for portable; otherwise what must exist, probed by DEP_PROBES in that script.
#             A leading '!' marks a dependency whose absence kills the gate outright rather than
#             costing it a half -- see fatal_deps(). Every dep of a `blocked` row is fatal.
